learning_outcomes.text: Students recognize the relationships in the system of modern and additive processes, assess the work result and analyze the interaction between input variables, effectiveness criteria and technological parameters.
Students have a complete and integrated knowledge of most core areas and fundamental aspects of manufacturing processes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and connections -> Delimitation of machining, additive and forming manufacturing processes, development of processes with regard to energy and sustainability aspects

Machining with geometrically defined cutting edges -> Movements, engagement and cutting parameters, cutting edge geometries, chip formation, chip types and chip shapes, forces, energy and power in machining, machining processes, cutting materials, cooling lubricant systems
Machining with geometrically undefined cutting edges -> Processes, calculation of effectiveness criteria, energy and power considerations
High-performance machining -> HPC and HSC milling, machining of hardened steels and hard metals, minimum quantity lubrication and dry machining

Additive manufacturing processes -> Process fundamentals and process variants, component development and support structures, construction of additive manufacturing systems, laser-based systems, efficiency potentials
Increasing efficiency in manufacturing processes -> Lean principles, automation, integration of digital technologies, determination and improvement of the CO2 footprint
Planning and calculating manufacturing sequences -> Combination possibilities of manufacturing processes, energy efficiency of a process linkage

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (Klausur) or oral exam (mündliche Prüfung)

assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is determined by the lecturers: written exam or oral examination. The ungraded examination performance is experimental work, consisting of approximately 3 to 5 experimental tasks.
